messages.content: Predict the decision of the participant in this public goods experiment. Three real participants make one contribution decision each. They sit at separate interconnected computer terminals and remain completely anonymous to one another. There are no previous rounds. Each person receives 20 points, with each point worth CHF 0.50. Each chooses how many points, from 0 to 20, to put into a shared public fund and keeps the remaining points. The experimenter DOUBLES the sum contributed by all three, then divides that doubled sum equally among all three people, regardless of their own contribution. Your final task earnings in points equal 20 minus your contribution plus two thirds of the sum of all three contributions. Cash earnings from this task are those points multiplied by CHF 0.50. Each contributed point therefore returns two thirds of a point to EACH member, while costing its contributor one point from their own endowment. You make this one-shot decision without knowing the other two people’s contributions. Written rules and comprehension examples explained the payoff calculation before choosing. Use only information available before this contribution decision. Output only the numerical contribution in points, without units or explanation.

You have your 20-point endowment and are anonymously grouped with two other participants. No choices or earnings of the other participants have been revealed. How many of your points do you contribute to the public fund?

They sit at separate interconnected computer terminals and remain completely anonymous to one another. There are no previous rounds. Each person receives 20 points, with each point worth CHF 0.50. Each chooses how many points, from 0 to 20, to put into a shared public fund and keeps the remaining points. The experimenter DOUBLES the sum contributed by all three, then divides that doubled sum equally among all three people, regardless of their own contribution. Your final task earnings in points equal 20 minus your contribution plus two thirds of the sum of all three contributions. Cash earnings from this task are those points multiplied by CHF 0.50. Each contributed point therefore returns two thirds of a point to EACH member, while costing its contributor one point from their own endowment. You make this one-shot decision without knowing the other two people’s contributions. Written rules and comprehension examples explained the payoff calculation before choosing. Use only information available before this contribution decision. Output only the numerical contribution in points, without units or explanation.
